summary.headline: Sapphire Foods Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11% to INR 790 mn with KFC SSSG at 4% (6% ex-Navratri) and restaurant EBITDA up 110 bps to 16.8% for KFC.
summary.overview: Management called Q4 FY26 its best quarter in 12 quarters on SSSG and adjusted EBITDA growth, driven by KFC consumer recruitment and Sri Lanka, despite LPG availability and inflation issues in India and Sri Lanka. Consolidated revenue grew 11% YoY in the quarter, while full-year revenue grew 8% and full-year adjusted EBITDA fell 9%. Consolidated PBT with exceptionals was negative INR 15.5 crore, including INR 6.2 crore Labour Code and INR 6.6 crore merger-related ESOP charges. Management said April trends were similar to Q4 for KFC, and the Devyani merger is targeted for completion by end of FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +10% YoY per transcript, margin down 20 bps
Exceptionals: INR 6.2 crore Labour Code, INR 6.6 crore merger-related ESOP modification

segments.name: KFC India
segments.commentary: Q4 SSSG 4% (6% ex-Navratri, highest in 14 quarters); FY26 revenue +11%, restaurant EBITDA 16.3% (down 100 bps); Q4 restaurant EBITDA 16.8% (+110 bps), gross margin +70 bps. 73 stores opened in FY26, total 575.

segments.name: Pizza Hut India
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue -6%, SSSG -7%, restaurant EBITDA down 6% on deleverage; FY26 revenue INR 507 crore (-7%), restaurant EBITDA -3.3% (down 570 bps). 7 stores opened in FY26, total 341. Tamil Nadu is the only market with double-digit SSSG and EBITDA growth.

segments.name: Sri Lanka (Pizza Hut)
segments.commentary: Q4 SSSG 11%, sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit SSSG; restaurant EBITDA margin 14.6% (down 20 bps) as minimum wage increases offset operating leverage. FY26 growth 16% in LKR, restaurant EBITDA 14.9% (down 50 bps); 9 stores opened, total 136.

guidance_outlook: Management said April trends are similar to Q4 for KFC, with positive SSSG, though Sri Lanka's Q1 is still evolving under LPG and fuel constraints.
Gross margin investment of 50-70 bps is expected if vendor-partner support for the INR 99 meal and BOGO offers is withdrawn.
Price increases: KFC about 1.5-2% cumulative; Pizza Hut about 2% in April; no further hikes planned unless raw material or oil prices rise sharply.
LPG cost increase of 25-40% could hit EBITDA by 30-50 bps for the group, per management.
Capex for FY27 expected similar to FY26 (about INR 320 crore in FY26 per analyst); KFC capex about INR 2.1-2.2 crore per store and Pizza Hut about INR 1.35-1.4 crore per store, excluding fees.
Devyani merger expected to complete by end of FY27: SEBI approval expected in 30-45 days, then NCLT (7-10 months) and CCI filing.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 99 value initiative rolled out across the network, especially North and West, and what is same-store transaction growth?
qa_highlights.answer: About 150 stores started Nov-Dec, about 200 by Jan-Mar, and all stores except Tamil Nadu by April; management calls it a permanent value layer, not a promotion. SSTG was said to be closer to SSSG in Q4, with no figure given.

qa_highlights.question: How much did marketing spend rise in KFC and will gross margin hold given the wider rollout?
qa_highlights.answer: Additional marketing of 75-100 bps of KFC sales. Gross margin held because vendor partners support the offer; if support is withdrawn, GM investment could be 50-70 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Have KFC restaurant margins bottomed and how confident is the company of mid-single-digit SSSG over the next couple of years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins should hold or improve as long as SSSG holds; Q3 and Q4 margins improved with SSSG. Confidence attributed to the strategy and April trends rather than a low base; rollout went from 150 to 220 to 400-plus stores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Sri Lanka in Q1 given LPG and fuel shortages, and is consumer discretionary spend weakening?
qa_highlights.answer: Quarter started well but LPG and fuel for transport remain difficult and evolving. April discretionary demand reasonable, with positive SSSG on a high base of double-digit growth for two years.

qa_highlights.question: Does April SSSG match Q4's 6% underlying rate, and is the Navratri shift a factor?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified that the 6% is the ex-Navratri Q4 figure, and April is trending at a similar underlying momentum; no April SSSG number was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY26 capex (about INR 320 crore per analyst) higher than store-level capex implies, and what is FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex includes refurbishment every 5-10 years and an annual renewal fee since the company completed 10 years; per-store capex KFC INR 2.1-2.2 crore and Pizza Hut INR 1.35-1.4 crore excluding fees; FY27 capex similar to FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is the strong KFC growth versus aggregator growth structural, and will brand growth converge with aggregators?
qa_highlights.answer: Dine-in and takeaway gap vs delivery has narrowed; own app and delivery have outgrown aggregators by a sizable margin. Aggregator growth in line with SSSG; management expects mix to stabilise over the long run but gave no timing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Devyani merger timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Registered office change approved by shareholders and authorities, formalities in about two weeks; SEBI approval expected in 30-45 days, then NCLT (7-10 months) and CCI filing in parallel; merger targeted by end of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact on bill value from the INR 99 and BOGO offers?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined APC impact of 2-3% from the offers; INR 99 meal drives higher transactions with lower APC; BOGO runs on select days and is margin-dilutive that day but accretive at restaurant EBITDA level.

capex_capacity: KFC store opened in Q4 FY26: 19 KFC, 2 Pizza Hut India and 3 Pizza Hut Sri Lanka; total restaurants 1,052 as of 31 Mar 2026.
FY26 openings: 73 KFC (total 575), 7 Pizza Hut India (total 341), 9 Pizza Hut Sri Lanka (total 136).
Capex per store excluding initial and renewal fees: KFC about INR 2.1-2.2 crore; Pizza Hut about INR 1.35-1.4 crore.
Capex has three components per management: new stores, refurbishment every 5-10 years, and renewal fee now kicking in as the company has completed 10 years; FY27 capex expected similar to FY26.
Pizza Hut India closed 15-20 stores in calendar 2025 while opening none in that year (per management, replacement openings partly explain capex gap vs. the INR 320 crore analyst figure).
Sri Lanka expansion: high single digit to low double digit store growth p.a. possible over next 2-3 years.
KFC digital kiosks live in 73% of restaurants; kiosks provide APC upside versus counter ordering.
demand_pricing: KFC Q4 SSSG 4%, 6% ex-Navratri (Navratri fully in March this year vs 2 days in March and 7 in April last year); highest in 14 quarters. Q4 revenue +15%, highest in 8 quarters.
KFC same-store transactions tracked closer to SSSG in Q4 (no figure given). Transactions ran 300-500 bps above SSSG in INR 99 offer stores, with bill value negative initially.

KFC value strategy: INR 99 Chicken Krisper Burger Meal in North and West (about 150 stores Nov-Dec, about 200 by Jan-Mar, all stores except Tamil Nadu from April); BOGO on select days in dine-in and takeaway in South. Additional marketing of 75-100 bps of KFC sales.
Gross margin: KFC GM +70 bps YoY, flat QoQ, supported by vendor partners (chicken, fries, beverage). Vendor support withdrawal could cost 50-70 bps GM.
KFC restaurant EBITDA Q4 16.8% (+110 bps); FY26 16.3% (-100 bps). Management says margin decline in FY26 was direct result of lack of SSSG over two years.
Pizza Hut India Q4 revenue -6%, SSSG -7%, GM +40 bps, restaurant EBITDA down 6% on deleverage; delivery 51% of mix. Tamil Nadu only market with double-digit SSSG and EBITDA growth.

Sri Lanka Q4 SSSG 11% (sixth straight double-digit quarter), revenue +15% in LKR and +16% in INR, GM +290 bps, restaurant EBITDA margin 14.6% (-20 bps) due to minimum wage hikes (two increases last year).

Pricing: KFC cumulative 1.5-2%; Pizza Hut about 2% in April. No further hikes planned unless raw material or oil prices rise sharply. Sri Lanka prices held well below inflation (about 50% vs 90-95% combined inflation over 18 months).
Dine-in and takeaway mix KFC 57% (stable YoY); Pizza Hut 49% dine-in/takeaway; Sri Lanka 62%.

April 2026: management says KFC trends similar to Q4 with positive SSSG; Sri Lanka quarter started well but LPG and fuel constraints evolving. Pizza Hut closures reduced from under 5% to under 3% of stores in April.
risks_watch: LPG availability and cost: 25-40% LPG cost rise could cut EBITDA 30-50 bps; Pizza Hut closures under 3% in April, KFC zero closures.
Withdrawal of vendor-partner support for INR 99 and BOGO offers could cost 50-70 bps gross margin.
Pizza Hut India continues to decline (Q4 revenue -6%, SSSG -7%, FY26 restaurant EBITDA -3.3%); turnaround depends on Tamil Nadu playbook scaling.
Sri Lanka margins under pressure from minimum wage increases; Q1 FY27 LPG and fuel constraints unresolved.
Sustainability of KFC SSSG against a high base of double-digit growth in Sri Lanka and reliance on value offers; KFC marketing spend up 75-100 bps.
Devyani merger approvals (SEBI, NCLT, CCI) and the Labour Code and ESOP charges (INR 6.2 crore and INR 6.6 crore) in Q4.
key_quotes: Q4 FY26 has been our best quarter in the last 12 quarters in terms of both SSSG and adjusted EBITDA growth.
This is not a promotion. I want to underline that this is not a promotion. This is a permanent value layer that we are building.
So, the drop of margin has been a direct result of lack of SSSG for last 2 years.
We have been quite cautious of expanding from 150 stores to 220 now to 400-plus stores.
summary.management_tone: Confident on KFC and Sri Lanka momentum and April trends, calling Q4 the best quarter in 12 quarters, but cautious on LPG availability, fuel costs, and the Sri Lanka Q1 outlook, which management said is still evolving. Management was evasive when asked about peer and sector comparisons, saying it had not seen the Eternal numbers and would wait for other results.

growth.why: Q4 consolidated revenue +11% and KFC SSSG +4% (6% ex-Navratri) with April trends similar to Q4; growth backed by 73 KFC openings in FY26, price increases of 1.5-2% and value offers, but no explicit FY27 revenue guidance and FY27 capex held similar to FY26 (~INR 320 crore per analyst).

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: KFC restaurant EBITDA up 110 bps to 16.8% in Q4 and management says margins hold or improve while SSSG holds, but vendor-support withdrawal could cost 50-70 bps GM and LPG cost rise of 25-40% could cut group EBITDA 30-50 bps.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: KFC added 73 stores in FY26 (total 575) and 19 in Q4 alone; FY27 capex guided similar to FY26 (~INR 320 crore per analyst), implying continued store openings at KFC ~INR 2.1-2.2 crore per store.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: KFC Q4 SSSG 4% (6% ex-Navratri) with April trends similar to Q4 and positive SSSG; transactions running 300-500 bps above SSSG in INR 99 offer stores, though Pizza Hut India SSSG is -7% and Sri Lanka Q1 is still evolving.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No explicit FY27 revenue or margin guidance was raised; management held capex flat and flagged 50-70 bps GM and 30-50 bps EBITDA headwinds, so upward revisions look unlikely near term.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Vendor-partner support for INR 99 and BOGO offers could be withdrawn (50-70 bps GM), LPG costs up 25-40% (30-50 bps EBITDA), and Sri Lanka Q1 is still evolving under LPG and fuel constraints after a six-quarter double-digit SSSG run.

rows.label: Price increases and no further hikes planned
rows.why: KFC cumulative 1.5-2% and Pizza Hut about 2% in April; management plans no further hikes unless raw material or oil prices rise sharply, with Sri Lanka prices held well below inflation (about 50% vs 90-95% combined inflation over 18 months).

rows.label: Sri Lanka store growth
rows.why: Management sees high single digit to low double digit store growth p.a. possible, from 136 stores after 9 openings in FY26 and 3 in Q4.

rows.label: Devyani merger completion by end FY27
rows.why: SEBI approval expected in 30-45 days, then NCLT (7-10 months) and CCI filing in parallel, with registered office change already approved by shareholders.

tone.note: Management was confident on KFC SSSG (4%, 6% ex-Navratri), April trends and Sri Lanka's double-digit run, but cautious on LPG, fuel costs and Sri Lanka Q1; analysts pushed on margin sustainability, SSTG disclosure and Pizza Hut's -7% SSSG, and management was evasive on peer comparisons.
